assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Esters
items.clue: Sweet-smelling compounds such as ethyl ethanoate.

items.label: Fermentation
items.clue: Sugar solution is converted to ethanol using yeast.

questions.stem: What is the functional group of the alkenes?

options.text: The –OH group found in alcohols
The –COOH group of the acids
The carbon–carbon double bond, C=C
A single carbon–carbon bond, C–C

questions.explanation: The specification gives the functional group of the alkenes as C=C.

questions.stem: Which functional group is found in every alcohol?

options.text: The carboxyl group, –COOH
The hydroxyl group, –OH
A carbon–carbon double bond
The hydroxide ion, OH⁻

questions.explanation: The specification states that alcohols contain the functional group -OH.

questions.stem: Which functional group do carboxylic acids contain?

options.text: The carboxyl group, –COOH
The hydroxyl group, –OH
A carbon–carbon double bond
The ester group, –COO–

questions.explanation: The specification gives the functional group of the carboxylic acids as -COOH.

questions.stem: Ethene, propene and butene all decolourise bromine water. What best explains this?

options.text: They share a functional group, so they react alike
Each one has its own reaction and the likeness is chance
They all contain the same number of carbon atoms
They just happen to react alike, with no shared reason

questions.explanation: It is the generality of reactions of functional groups that determines the reactions of organic compounds.

questions.stem: Which list gives the first four members of the homologous series of alcohols?

options.text: Methanol, ethanol, propanol and pentanol
Ethanol, propanol, butanol, pentanol
Methane, ethanol, propanol and butanol
Methanol, ethanol, propanol and butanol

questions.explanation: These are the four alcohols named in the specification.

questions.stem: Which list gives the first four members of the homologous series of carboxylic acids?

options.text: Ethanoic, propanoic, butanoic, pentanoic acid
Methanoic, ethanoic, propanoic and butanoic acid
Methanol, ethanol, propanol and butanol
Methanoic, ethanoic, propanoic, pentanoic acid

questions.explanation: These are the four carboxylic acids named in the specification.

questions.stem: How do alkenes tend to burn in air?

options.text: They combine with the nitrogen of the air as well as the oxygen
They do not burn at all, as the double bond is stable
With smoky flames, because combustion is incomplete
With smoky flames, because the oxygen supply is too great

questions.explanation: The specification states that alkenes tend to burn in air with smoky flames because of incomplete combustion.

questions.stem: Ethanol can be represented as CH₃CH₂OH. What does this form show?

options.text: Only the total number of atoms of each element
The –OH group and how the carbon atoms are grouped
Every bond in the molecule, drawn in full
That ethanol releases hydroxide ions in water

questions.explanation: This form sets out the groups in the molecule, so the functional group can be picked out.

questions.stem: Ethanoic acid can be represented as CH₃COOH. What does this form show?

options.text: An –OH group on a chain of two carbons
A –COOH group joined to a CH₃ group
Every bond of the acid, drawn out
Just the atom count, like C₂H₄O₂

questions.explanation: Writing it this way separates the carboxyl group from the rest of the molecule.

questions.stem: Ethene is burned in plenty of air. What are the products of complete combustion?

options.text: Carbon dioxide and soot
Carbon dioxide and hydrogen
Carbon monoxide and hydrogen
Carbon dioxide and water

questions.explanation: Alkenes react with oxygen in combustion reactions in the same way as other hydrocarbons.

questions.stem: A displayed formula of ethanol is drawn instead of writing CH₃CH₂OH. What does the drawing add?

options.text: It shows nothing new about the ethanol molecule
It shows every bond, including the O–H bond
It shows how many molecules are in the sample
It shows the charge on each atom present

questions.explanation: A displayed formula shows all of the bonds in the molecule, which the written form does not.

questions.stem: Ethanoic acid is added to sodium carbonate. What happens?

options.text: It fizzes as vigorously as dilute hydrochloric acid does
There is no reaction, since it is only a weak acid
A white precipitate forms and the mixture clouds
It fizzes and carbon dioxide gas is given off

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to release carbon dioxide, as other acids do.

questions.stem: Why is ethanoic acid described as a weak acid?

options.text: All of its molecules ionise in aqueous solution
Only some of its molecules ionise in solution
Its solutions are dilute rather than concentrated
It ionises completely but only very slowly

questions.explanation: A weak acid is only partially ionised in aqueous solution.

questions.stem: Solutions of hydrochloric acid and ethanoic acid have the same concentration. How do their pH values compare?

options.text: Ethanoic acid has the lower pH of the two
Both have the same pH, as both are acids
Ethanoic acid has a pH of more than 7
Ethanoic acid has the higher pH of the two

questions.explanation: It ionises only partially, so its solution has a lower concentration of H+ ions and a higher pH.
